assessment.nobel_worthiness: A new therapeutic modality built on a clear molecular design principle: bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues hijack E3 ligases to eliminate rather than inhibit a target protein, giving precise control over recognition and reaching proteins once called undruggable. The shift from occupancy-driven to event-driven pharmacology changed what chemists and clinicians can do, and the field now spans academia and industry.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies founded the PROTAC concept (2001), and Ciulli made the VHL ligand and structural-mechanistic ternary-complex work that made PROTACs drug-like. The thalidomide/cereblon molecular-glue discovery (Handa, Ito) and Gray's degrader chemistry are a second strand that a three-person limit cannot fully honor.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of work, multiple degraders in clinical trials, and independent validation across many labs. Timely, though clinical approval is still pending, which some members may consider premature.
uncertainties: Whether credit is fairly split between the PROTAC concept and the cereblon glue mechanism
Absence of an approved PROTAC drug at the time of assessment
Ordering of Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli versus Handa and Ito is not resolved by the supplied credit

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are a chemical solution to the delivery problem for siRNA and mRNA: pH-responsive lipids that encapsulate nucleic acids, escape endosomes and enable medicines. The technology enabled patisiran and the COVID-19 mRNA vaccines, a rare case of molecular design with enormous clinical reach, and it is directly relevant to nanomaterial-biology interfaces.
assessment.attribution: The Vancouver group (Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan) developed ionizable lipids and rapid-mixing formulation; Anderson and Langer developed combinatorial lipidoid libraries. Credit is spread across several groups and companies, and a three-person selection leaves out meaningful contributors.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at global scale and independently reproduced, so impact is not in doubt. The 2023 Medicine prize went to nucleoside modification, which makes recognition of the delivery chemistry timely rather than premature.
uncertainties: Fair allocation among the Vancouver and Cambridge lines of work
Whether the committee regards this as chemistry or pharmaceutical technology
Patent and commercial disputes may blur the scientific attribution

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Sequencing-by-synthesis with reversible terminator chemistry and single-molecule clustering made DNA sequencing massively parallel and cheap, transforming biology and medicine. The decisive steps were chemical: engineered nucleotides, cleavable linkers and surface chemistry. The lasting impact is among the largest of any analytical method in the last thirty years.
assessment.attribution: Balasubramanian and Klenerman conceived and developed the Solexa chemistry; Mayer and Ju contributed related reversible-terminator and cluster concepts, and Rothberg led pyrosequencing-based 454 and Ion Torrent. A two-person prize fits Solexa best, but credit for the field overall is contested among competing platforms.
assessment.maturity: Mature and universally adopted for roughly two decades, with decades of independent confirmation. Recognition is arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Which of the competing platform inventors should share credit
Whether Illumina-style chemistry alone represents the whole discovery
Whether the committee sees this as chemistry rather than genomics instrumentation

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetic code expansion uses orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs to install non-canonical amino acids site-specifically in living cells, giving chemists atomic-level control over protein composition. It underpins protein labeling, photo-crosslinking, biomaterials and therapeutic proteins, and it is a clean molecular design principle with wide reach into biomedicine.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang established the first eukaryotic and bacterial orthogonal systems; Chin extended the concept to eukaryotes, multiple codons and whole-genome recoded organisms. Mehl and Yokoyama contributed significant systems and structures. A three-person group is plausible, though the borders of contribution are debated.
assessment.maturity: More than twenty years of independent replication and broad commercial and academic use, so maturity is high.
uncertainties: Whether Chin or Wang should be preferred when the prize is limited to three people
Overlap with directed evolution and other protein-engineering prizes already awarded
Relative weight of Yokoyama and Mehl is uncertain

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reading single DNA or RNA molecules electrically through protein nanopores is a distinctive analytical chemistry achievement. It started as single-molecule sensing with engineered pores and became portable long-read sequencing, and the same sensing principle extends to peptides, small molecules and diagnostics.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Brandin, Branton and Deamer showed that polynucleotides translocate through alpha-hemolysin; Bayley engineered the pores and sensing chemistry; Akeson achieved enzymatic ratcheting and strand sequencing. Branton and Deamer share the early idea, so allocation of credit is intricate and one person (Branton) is also credited.
assessment.maturity: The technique is commercially deployed and independently validated, though continued improvements in accuracy and the protein-sequencing extension are still in progress.
uncertainties: How to apportion credit between the founding concept and the engineered pore and motor chemistry
Whether sequencing performance alone is enough relative to Illumina-style approaches
Competing contributions from Oxford Nanopore engineers are not credited in the list

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors chemically convert one DNA base to another without a double-strand break by fusing deaminases to a CRISPR-guided protein, and the evolved adenine base editors were found by directed evolution. It is chemistry applied directly to the genome and is entering therapeutic use, which is exactly the route from molecular design to clinical impact.
assessment.attribution: Liu led the conceptual and engineering effort, with Komor and Gaudelli as lead trainees on the cytosine and adenine editors. Nishida and Kondo reported a parallel cytosine deaminase system, but a single-laureate prize for Liu is the cleanest configuration.
assessment.maturity: Roughly ten years old, with early clinical results emerging and strong independent adoption. Somewhat young for recognition, and it overlaps with the 2020 CRISPR prize.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views this as too close to the 2020 CRISPR prize
Long-term clinical safety and efficacy are not yet established
Credit for the independent Nishida and Kondo work

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Programming nanoparticle assembly with DNA, and the spherical nucleic acid architecture, gives sequence-controlled recognition on a nanomaterial surface. It supports colorimetric diagnostics, intracellular gene regulation, and crystal engineering, and it represents a core principle linking gold nanoparticles with biomolecular recognition.
assessment.attribution: Mirkin and colleagues (including Mucic and Storhoff) reported DNA-gold nanoparticle aggregates in 1996, and Alivisatos independently reported DNA-nanocrystal organization at the same time. The two groups' concurrent work supports a two-person configuration, though Mirkin's later spherical nucleic acid work is the larger body.
assessment.maturity: Almost thirty years of replication, with commercial diagnostics in use, but clinical therapeutic uses of spherical nucleic acids are still modest.
uncertainties: Relative credit of Mirkin versus Alivisatos for the founding observation
Therapeutic translation has not yet been broadly proven
The group has a larger set of contributors than a three-person prize can include

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation lets chemists stitch unprotected peptide segments through a chemoselective thioester-cysteine reaction, enabling total chemical synthesis and semisynthesis of proteins with defined modifications. It gave access to homogeneous glycoproteins, ubiquitinated proteins and modified histones that cannot be obtained otherwise.
assessment.attribution: Dawson, Muir, Kent and Kent's chemical-ligation precursors established the reaction in 1994, and Muir later developed expressed protein ligation for semisynthesis. Danishefsky, Brik and Liu extended it to glycoprotein and ubiquitin chemistry. Credit is cleanly traceable to Kent, Dawson and Muir.
assessment.maturity: More than thirty years of independent use and validation, so maturity is high, though its prize-level impact is somewhat narrower than the platforms ranked above it.
uncertainties: Impact is mostly among specialist chemical biologists, compared with broad clinical use
Whether Danishefsky and others should displace Dawson
Overlap with earlier peptide synthesis prizes
